page: Microsoft Azure D48pds_v5 is an ARM64-based virtual machine belonging to the DPDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of an 1843 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks show a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves strong multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and software compilation using Clang, alongside high-throughput Redis SET operations at 61.96 million operations per second. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1121.0 and a weak single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 8.9 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 175.53 GB/sec for large block read-only operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture offers high resource density and dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, making it a viable option for scale-out workloads that benefit from parallel execution. The bundled 1843 GB local SSD provides high-capacity storage without requiring external attachments. This server is suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, Redis caching layers, database operations, and static web serving, while it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM prompt processing.
